who_for: An air purifier helps if you deal with allergies, pet dander, wildfire smoke, or cooking odors. It works best in the room where you spend the most time, usually a bedroom or living room, running continuously.
Size it to the room. A purifier that's too small for the space will barely change the air no matter what filter it uses.

how_we_picked.label: CADR and coverage
how_we_picked.text: Clean Air Delivery Rate measures how fast a purifier cleans the air. We matched each unit's CADR to realistic room sizes rather than the optimistic maximum on the box.

how_we_picked.label: True HEPA filtration
how_we_picked.text: We favored sealed True HEPA filters, which capture at least 99.97% of particles 0.3 microns in size. We avoided purifiers that depend on ionizers or ozone to clean the air; where a pick has an ionizer, it can be switched off.

how_we_picked.label: Noise
how_we_picked.text: A purifier only helps when it's running, so we weighed how quiet it is on a setting that still moves meaningful air, especially for bedrooms.

how_we_picked.label: Filter cost
how_we_picked.text: Replacement filters can cost more than the purifier over a few years, so we factored in yearly filter prices.

how_we_picked.label: Smart features
how_we_picked.text: Air-quality sensors and an auto mode are useful. App control is a bonus, not a requirement.
